data.name: Ashmay
data.gender_notes: Ashmay is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Ashmay is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Ash’ meaning immortal and ‘May’ meaning illusion. This name is associated with the idea of eternal consciousness, beyond the illusion of physical existence. The name Ashmay carries the meaning “Ash - immortal, May - illusion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashmay usually hope their child will grow to embody ash - immortal, may - illusion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey towards self-realization and enlightenment, beyond the illusory nature of physical existence.
data.etymology: Ashmay belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ash - immortal, May - illusion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashmay total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ashmay holds a deep cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is derived from the ancient Sanskrit language. The name carries the weight of centuries-old traditions and beliefs. In Hindu mythology, Ash represents the eternal and immortal aspect of existence, while May signifies illusion or the temporary nature of the material world. This dichotomy reflects the Hindu philosophy of dualism, where physical reality and the eternal soul are interconnected yet distinct.
data.spiritual_significance: Ashmay is a powerful name with deep spiritual significance. It signifies the eternal essence of an individual's consciousness beyond the physical body and the temporary world. Ashmay represents the ultimate reality, which is beyond the illusory world of senses and teaches us to seek the truth beyond the physical plane. The name encourages self-reflection, introspection, and the pursuit of spiritual growth, reminding us of the importance of our immortal souls.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ashmay: The one who is free from fear and grief, embracing the infinite peace of the universe within.

historical_references.reference: Ashmay is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata as a Rishi (sage), son of Rishi Atri and Anasuya. He is known for his immense knowledge and piety.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It provides ancient narratives of the history, traditional culture, ethics, and spirituality of ancient India.

historical_references.reference: Ashmay is also mentioned in the Puranic texts as a sage who performed severe penance to gain the boon of having a celestial child. He is said to have been the father of Sage Agastya, who later became a significant figure in Tamil literature and folk traditions.
historical_references.context: Puranas are a genre of Indian literature which focus on ancient Hindu legends, history, philosophy, and tradition.
